convoLines.text: "What got you through the first week? The very first days."
"Look — Shock's underrated. It's the body's way of buying you time."
"This one — Sugar Maple. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Work. I just worked — fixed things, carried things, dug. If my hands were busy my head couldn't do the math on what we'd lost."
"Still on what got you through the first week."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Have you heard what they're calling Hushpuppy? Duc is pushing 'Big-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."
"The fire'll settle it. It settles everything, eventually."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Do you still sing? ...Sorry — weird question. I just realized I haven't heard anyone sing."
"Hah. Ha! The creek concerts. I've heard those. Keep going."
"Under my breath, when I'm working. Old songs from Mumbai, India. The words are half gone but the tune holds. Tunes outlast everything. That's where we are."
"Still on whether you still sing."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "The whole fire was arguing about Hushpuppy last night — what to even CALL it. 'Ugly-Eyes' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Alright, duty calls. This was a good pause."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"You said shock got you through the first week. Just kept moving. What's carrying you now?"
"Take your time."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"Yeah? What's up?"

"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "The whole fire was arguing about Hushpuppy last night — what to even CALL it. 'Ugly-Eyes' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"It's all right if you don't know."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Staghorn Sumac — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You've been singing in the creek. Badly, by your own admission. Heard anything worth stealing yet?"
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
It's quiet at the hollow. Fatima doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Can I tell you something? I saw something in the woods I'm not telling anyone about."
"...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Since Riley died... I keep expecting to see Riley at the fire. Stupid."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "I'd follow you out past the treeline. Don't tell the others — they'd want to come too."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on each other. Worth considering."
You show them Dandelion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Actually, forget it."

"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.' We still owe that personal stuff a proper ending, too."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"I check everyone's shoes for wear for Riley, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
"Like I said — Still on what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You're one of the good ones. Don't make me regret saying that out loud." "That's where we are."
You show them Staghorn Sumac — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Actually, forget it."
"Look — We never did finish talking about that personal stuff — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? 'Sure — what's on your mind?'"
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
You walk to the ridge with Fatima. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
Another crack. The telling doesn't hold together anymore.
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? I know who took the extra rations but won't say."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
Counted.
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"
"Hardened Duel. They just... took Fatima. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Anyway — I should get going."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

deathBeat: d10: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Riley Taylor is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d10: 🕯️ Riley Taylor is dead — sickness. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
recoverHome: d11: That night, they bring Riley home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d10: ◈ SYSTEM: "Ooh. NEIGHBORS. You know what neighbors are for? STORYLINES. Go knock — worst case, it's CONTENT. Best case? The show gets BIGGER."
d12: ◈ AUDIENCE TRIAL — SYSTEM: "The audience wants an encore. A trial, then — smaller this time, but televised." Haul 1,000 kcal to the pantry within 3 days. Reward: integration, and a lesson.
